verified_clean: All {placeholders} identical to English across 270 items (programmatically checked on drafts and repairs). Negations ('ha di a amiwa', 'ha di ke', 'Se ke wa', 'ha ho letho le hlakotsweng', 'e seng') preserved. Recover (Aha hape) is distinct from View (Sheba), Create (Etsa) and Retry (Leka hape). Sold/Picked/Spent distinguished; buyer 'moreki' vs supplier 'mofani' distinct. No isiZulu/Xitsonga/Tshivenda words found in the drafts.
confidence_limits: I am a machine reviewer, not a fluent Sesotho speaker's approval. My Sesotho is good for grammar and common vocabulary but weaker on agricultural/finance register, noun-class concord in long sentences, and regional (Lesotho vs South African) orthography. Repairs are suggestions and should also be checked by a native speaker. 'ok' means no meaning error found, not that the wording is natural. The A-file usage strings leak code and English fragments, so Phase A was not perfectly blind.
